Definition: from G1074 and G3056; to reckon by generations, i.e. trace in genealogy:--count by descent.
BiblicalUsage: Genealogéō means to reckon by generations, to trace a line of descent. It occurs just once, in Hebrews 7:6, where Melchizedek, whose descent is not counted from the Levites, still received tithes from Abraham.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the point is the descent that does not count: Melchizedek stands outside the Levitical line, and that is exactly why he points to Christ.
